newsitem.title: USA: First Southeast revises FY96 earnings down.
newsitem.headline: First Southeast revises FY96 earnings down.

text.p: First Southeast Financial Corp said on Friday it had revised its earnings for the fiscal year ended June 30 down to $939,000 from the $1.1 million reported earlier because of dividend accounting.

"The reduction in earnings is directly related to the final determination of the portion of the company's recent $10 per share special cash dividend which will be treated as a return of capital," the company said in a statement.
Tax advisors determined that 53.76 percent of the distribution would be treated as an ordinary dividend and 46.24 percent as a return of capital, the company said.

Since the ordinary dividend portion was less than originally estimated, the amount of tax deductible dividend paid on shares in the company's employee stock ownership plan had been cut by $480,000, First Southeast said.
The revised earnings reflected the company's subsequent $166,000 income tax increase, it said.
Shareholders should consult their tax advisors regarding their individual situations, the company said.
